newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson, Home Depot, Tiffany earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson, Home Depot, Tiffany earnings rise.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp., Tiffany & Co. and Home Depot Inc. Tuesday reported robust profits for the second quarter, but results were sluggish at specialty retailers AnnTaylor Stores Corp. and Limited Inc.
The results showed inventory management, cost cutting and a strong economy have lifted most retailers, although fashion missteps have hurt some apparel chains.
Retail earnings for the second quarter have been "in line to slightly ahead of expectations," said Wayne Hood of Prudential Securities.

At Dayton Hudson Corp., parent of Target discount stores, net income rose to $130 million, or 54 cents a share, during the second quarter ended Aug. 2, vs. $101 million, or 42 cents a share during the same period a year ago. Revenues rose to $6.3 billion from $5.8 billion a year earlier.

This year's results included a charge of $11 million, or 5 cents a share, for debt redemption. Excluding the charge, earnings reached 59 cents a share, surpassing analysts' average estimate of 55 cents a share as compiled by research firm First Call.
The Minneapolis-based company's 769 Target discount stores had pretax earnings of $274 million, up 14 percent. Target's same-store sales, or sales of stores open a year, rose 6 percent.
Dayton Hudson's stock fell $1 to $59.69 on the New York Stock Exchange. Analysts said the decline reflected disappointment with expenses tied to the expansion of Target's private-label credit card.

Home Depot, the Atlanta-based home improvement supply retailer, said earnings rose to $358 million, or 48 cents a share during the second quarter from $270 million, or 37 cents a share in the same period last year. Sales rose 24 percent to $6.6 billion.
The results marked the 46th consecutive quarter of record earnings per share for Home Depot. Analysts had expected a smaller rise in earnings to 46 cents a share.

"They have had a history of being able more often than not to meet or exceed expectations," said Donald Spindel of A.G. Edwards & Sons. "It's basically a situation where their execution is better than the others."

He noted the company's same-store sales rose 5 percent, but its earnings per share jumped 30 percent. Lowe's Cos. Inc., Home Depot's nearest competitor, said on Monday that same-store sales rose 3 percent and earnings rose 9 percent.
Home Depot stock climbed $1.44 to $49.44 on the NYSE.
Tony jeweler Tiffany & Co. said its earnings increased to $10.4 million, or 29 cents a share, from $8.2 million, or 24 cents a share. Sales rose 7 percent to $217.1 million.
Analysts had predicted Tiffany would earn 28 cents a share, and the company's stock gained $2.25 to $43, also on the NYSE.
Analysts said Tiffany has been successful in its bid to attract less affluent customers, noting advertisements for diamond rings with prices starting at $850.
"They've reached out to a broader base of consumers without damaging their franchise," said Barbara Miller of Alex. Brown & Sons Inc.
Limited said its net income fell to $27.6 million, or 10 cents a share during the quarter from $33.2 million, or 12 cents a share a year earlier. Sales rose 7 percent to $2 billion.

The decline in profits, which had been expected on Wall Street, reflected the problems the Ohio-based retailer has had finding the right mix of fashions for its Limited and Express apparel chains, analysts said. The company's stock fell 6.25 cents to $22.44 on the NYSE.

AnnTaylor said earnings rose to $812,000, or 3 cents a share during the second quarter, from $627,000, or 3 cents a share a year earlier. Earnings per share were flat because the company's average shares outstanding rose 11 percent.
Sales fell about 2 percent to $185 million.

The results reflected an extraordinary loss of 1 cent a share, the company said. Excluding the loss, earnings were 4 cents a share, in line with Wall Street estimates. Last month, AnnTaylor warned its results for the second quarter would be eak due to poor sales in June.
AnnTaylor's stock closed unchanged at $17.375 on the NYSE.
